A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phase fluctuations are the key ingredients in the pseudo-gap state of the underdopped cuprates, as well as the superconducting state.
superconducting fluctuations in underdoped cuprate materials can be detected by INS experiments, but are not detected by NMR experiments.
the phase fluctuations in the pseudo-gap phase are very similar to the phase fluctuations in a conventional superconductor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phase fluctuations in the pseudo-gap phase of the underdoping cuprates are as important as the pseudo-gap itself.
phase fluctuations in the pseudo-gap state can explain the observed suppression of $1/T_2$ in NMR and the appearance of the resonance peak in INS, without any need to invoke a spin-gap.
the pseudo-gap phase of the cuprates is a {\it phase fluctuating superconductor}.
